name: skytrax-reviews-dataset
what_it_holds: Four committed CSVs scraped from airlinequality.com (Skytrax): 41,396 airline reviews, 17,721 airport reviews, 2,264 lounge reviews, 1,258 seat reviews, with rating dimensions (comfort, cleanliness, staff, amenities). Scraped as of Aug 2, 2015. CC0-1.0 license on the repo (scrape legality of underlying site noted as ambiguous by author). 73 stars/41 forks.
why_useful: Text/sentiment travel-demand proxy adjacent to Airbnb (traveler experience/sentiment on air travel) - could feed a text-based travel-demand sentiment index (gap 14 adjacent) though it is a one-time 2015 scrape, not updated, so limited as a current indicator; more useful as a methodology template for scraping airline-review sentiment than as current data.

name: gtfs-hub
what_it_holds: Aggregation/enhancement pipeline for German public transit GTFS feeds, gathered from CUTR-at-USF/awesome-transit list. Produces enhanced GTFS feeds for German transit agencies.
why_useful: A one-command pull method for German ground-transport capacity data (gap 10 mentions DB/rail capacity generally); minor incremental value since it's a processing pipeline for transit schedules, not passenger volumes.

name: The Mobility Database (GTFS catalogue)
what_it_holds: Repository/catalogue of 2000+ mobility (transit GTFS) datasets worldwide, successor to OpenMobilityData; linked from CUTR-at-USF/awesome-transit on GitHub. Not itself a GitHub-hosted data store but a discovery index for transit schedule/GTFS feeds globally, many of which are mirrored on GitHub by individual agencies/maintainers.
why_useful: A discovery tool (like the CKAN/Socrata discovery clients gap 17 asks for) to find ground-transportation capacity data by city/country as an ABNB travel-volume cross-check; breadth is high but each underlying feed needs individual vetting.

name: CapMetrics
what_it_holds: Historical archive of Austin, TX transit (Capital Metro) vehicle position/ridership-adjacent data, per its listing in CUTR-at-USF/awesome-transit. Austin is one of the 13 cities in our Inside Airbnb panel.
why_useful: A local ground-transport activity series for Austin that could be cross-checked against Inside Airbnb Austin listings/calendar activity as a market-level travel-volume proxy (gap 10), though scope and freshness need verification before use.

name: OpenFlights airport/airline/route database
what_it_holds: Static reference tables of world airports, airlines, and routes (not schedules/volumes), maintained as flat files linkable from GitHub mirrors; catalogued in awesomedata/awesome-public-datasets/Transportation. Widely mirrored on GitHub (e.g. jpatokal/openflights).
why_useful: A reference/join table (airport-to-city, route existence) rather than a volume series; could support building an airline-capacity proxy for gap 10 when paired with a real traffic source (e.g. BTS T-100), but on its own has no time-series volume.
